decisions.boundary_taylor_bridge: ROUND-5 RE-PLAN OF THE CELL TAYLOR STEP (F1.5 flag FLAG-boundary-taylor; fix-locus = this plan). The claimed DIRECT reuse of `Causalean.Stat.Nonparametric.holder_taylor_monomial_approx` for the cubic Taylor steps (C5) and (C9) of thm:primitive-endpoint-concentration, and for the one-dimensional propensity expansion (C11), is WITHDRAWN. Signature re-read in source (Approximation/HolderTaylorMonomial.lean:316-328): the lemma requires a SYMMETRIC closed sup-norm cube `{x | forall i, |x i - x0 i| <= r} subseteq S` (hypothesis `hS`) together with `0 < h < r`, and it controls the error only on the symmetric cube `{x0 + h . u : |u_j| <= 1}`. The learner's cells are ONE-SIDED boxes `I_j x K_l = x0 + [0,h)^2` anchored at their LOWER-LEFT corner, and the Taylor centre `gamma^0_{aj,l}` of (C6) is the expansion at that corner. For every cell meeting the boundary of `[0,1]^2` -- `j = 0`, `l = 0`, `l = J-1`, and decisively the TERMINAL cell `x0 = (1-h, 1-h)` which is the whole point of the theorem -- the two requirements are jointly unsatisfiable under `HolderBallStd . 4 20 ([0,1]^2)` alone: a symmetric cube of radius `r > h` centred at a corner-anchored `x0` leaves the unit square, so `hS` forces `r <= h` and contradicts `h < r`. The lemma is therefore not a clean total fit and is NOT invoked anywhere in this plan. REPLACEMENT (build-inline, no gate, no strengthening of the paper's assumption): Helpers/BoundaryTaylor.lean proves a LOCAL ONE-SIDED / RECTANGULAR boundary Taylor lemma DERIVED FROM THE STATED HOLDER CONDITION, in the derivative-within formulation that remains valid up to and including the boundary. Three steps, all confirmed Mathlib-reachable this round: (i) `holderBallStd_within_of_convex` -- on a convex closed `S` with nonempty interior (here the unit cube), `HolderBallStd f 4 L S` implies the SAME two bounds with `iteratedFDerivWithin R j f S` in place of the global `iteratedFDeriv`, at EVERY point of `S` including boundary points: at interior points the two agree (`iteratedFDerivWithin_of_isOpen` on `interior S` plus `iteratedFDerivWithin_congr_set` / `iteratedFDerivWithin_eq_iteratedFDeriv`), `ContDiffOn.continuousOn_iteratedFDerivWithin` (with `uniqueDiffOn_convex`) makes the within-derivative continuous on `S`, and `Convex.closure_interior_eq_closure_of_nonempty_interior` makes the interior dense in `S`, so the bounds pass to the limit; (ii) `cellLineTaylor` -- for `x0 in S` and a direction `y` with the whole segment `x0 + [0,1] . y` inside `S` (automatic for a one-sided cell by convexity, boundary cells included), the line restriction `phi s = f (x0 + s . y)` is `ContDiffOn R 3` on `Icc 0 1` by composition with the affine map (`ContDiffOn.comp`, `ContinuousLinearMap.iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_right`, `iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_add_left'`, `uniqueDiffOn_Icc_zero_one`), so Mathlib's `taylor_mean_remainder_lagrange` at order 2 applies WITHOUT any global smooth extension, and step (i) turns the Lagrange remainder into `(L/3!) * ||y||^4`; (iii) `cellMonomialApprox` -- the diagonal Taylor polynomial is re-indexed into the fixed 10-monomial (resp. 4-monomial) basis, giving coefficients `theta` with `sup_{u in [0,1]^d} |f (x0 + h . u) - sum_k theta_k * u^{e_k}| <= C_d * L * h^4`, instantiated at `d = 2` for (C5) and (C9) and at `d = 1` for (C11). ADAPTATION REFERENCE for F3: Approximation/HolderTaylorMonomial.lean itself -- its private `holder_line_taylor`, `holder_diag_diff_le`, `diagonal_expansion`, `indexCount` carry exactly this proof pattern; the two gaps to bridge are (a) its global-extension step `exists_global_contDiff_of_contDiffOn`, which needs an OPEN `U subseteq S` and hence fails on the boundary, replaced by the within-derivative route (i), and (b) its symmetric-cube geometry replaced by the one-sided box `x0 + [0,h]^d`. The private helpers cannot be called directly, so the file is a re-derivation at ~550 lines, elementary throughout. ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: an explicit `C^{3,1}` extension bridge (Hestenes reflection `ftilde(t,x) = sum_{k=1..4} c_k f(-t/k, x)` in each coordinate with Vandermonde coefficients, plus corner composition, or a Whitney extension) would let the library lemma be called verbatim, but it either enlarges the Holder radius beyond the fixed constant 20 that the paper's class pins (changing `P_4`) or demands a 600-1000 line reflection construction with hyperplane and corner gluing; the within-derivative route needs no extension at all and keeps the assumption exactly as the paper states it. SCOPE OF THE FIX: this replacement is applied identically to the hazard Taylor step (C5), the `q_a = S_a g_a` terminal-cell step (C9), and the one-dimensional propensity step (C11); no other node's disposition moves, and no new gate is introduced.

env.world: A quadratic-endpoint censored-survival experiment on the unit square. A unit carries a covariate \(X\in[0,1]\) with Lebesgue density \(f\), a binary treatment \(A\in\{0,1\}\) with propensity \(\pi_1(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x)\) and \(\pi_a(x)=a\pi_1(x)+(1-a)\{1-\pi_1(x)\}\), two potential event times \(T(0),T(1)\in[0,\infty]\) whose conditional hazards are \(\lambda_a(t,x)\) with survivals \(S_a(t\mid x)=\exp\{-\int_0^t\lambda_a(v,x)\,dv\}\), and a censoring time \(C\in[0,1]\) whose conditional survival factors exactly as \(G_a(t\mid x)=(1-t)^2g_a(t,x)\) for \(t<1\) with \(G_a(1\mid x)=0\) and \(g_a(0,x)=1\). The realized event time is \(T=T(A)\); only the coarsened unit \(O=(X,A,U,\Delta)\) with \(U=\min\{T,C\}\in[0,1)\) and \(\Delta=\mathbf 1\{T\le C\}\) is observed. Attached to the observed unit are the counting process \(N(t)=\mathbf 1\{U\le t,\Delta=1\}\), the at-risk process \(Y_{\mathrm{risk}}(t)=\mathbf 1\{U\ge t\}\), the event martingale \(M_a(t)=N(t)-\int_0^tY_{\mathrm{risk}}(v)\lambda_a(v,X)\,dv\) on \(\{A=a\}\), and the rescaled at-risk function \(q_a(t,x)=S_a(t\mid x)g_a(t,x)\). A diagnostic margin \(\delta\in(0,1)\) and the shorter horizon \(\tau=1-\delta\) are fixed constants of the in-class sanity check only.

env.world: The radius-\(20\) isotropic Hölder primitive class and the fixed-horizon RMST target. The norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{C^{3,1}}\) is the maximum of the suprema of derivatives through order three and the Lipschitz seminorms of the third derivatives, and \(\mathcal H^4_{20}(\mathcal X)=\{h:\lVert h\rVert_{C^{3,1}(\mathcal X)}\le20\}\). The primitive class \(\mathcal P_4\) collects the laws satisfying the causal-structural, band, exact-quadratic-censoring and three radius-\(20\) Hölder conditions; \(\mathcal P_4^{\circ}\) is its interior subclass, cut out by positivity of the interior-slack functional \(\rho_{\mathrm{int}}\). The target is the causal restricted-mean contrast \(\theta=\theta_1-\theta_0\) with \(\theta_a=E_P[m_a(X)]\) and \(m_a(x)=\int_0^1S_a(v\mid x)\,dv\); the remaining-life weight is \(H_a(t,x)=S_a(t\mid x)^{-1}\int_t^1S_a(v\mid x)\,dv\), the arm influence component is \(D_a\), the contrast influence function is \(D=D_1-D_0\), and the influence variance is \(V_P=E_P[D(O)^2]\). The law \(P^{\star}\) is the explicit interior witness whose feasible score has a \(5/2\) moment but no third moment.

env.world: The two-fold cross-fitted endpoint learner and its Wald inference. On a training sample of size \(M\) the resolution is \(J_M=\max\{1,\lfloor(M/\log(M+2))^{1/12}\rfloor\}\) with bandwidth \(h_M=J_M^{-1}\) and primitive rate \(r_M=h_M^4+\sqrt{\log(M+2)/(Mh_M^4)}+\log(M+2)/(Mh_M^4)\). The learner returns the foldwise nuisance triple \(\widehat\eta=(\widehat\pi_a,\widehat\lambda_a,\widehat g_a)_{a=0,1}\), from which \(\widehat S_a,\widehat G_a,\widehat H_a,\widehat m_a\) are formed by the same formulas as their population counterparts; a generic in-band triple \(\bar\eta=(\bar\pi_a,\bar\lambda_a,\bar g_a)_{a=0,1}\) with derived \(\bar S_a,\bar G_a,\bar H_a,\bar m_a\) is the argument of the integrated one-step score \(\psi_a\). A deterministic fold map \(k:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,2\}\) assigns each unit its contribution \(W_i\); the total estimator is \(\widehat\theta\) and the nonnegative variance estimator is \(\widehat V\). Inference uses the standard normal distribution function \(\Phi\), a nominal error probability \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the quantile \(z_{1-\alpha/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\), and the Wald interval \(\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\).
